OpenAI just made a move that changes how every business should think about AI costs.

The new GPT-5.6 family ships as three separate models — not one. Sol handles flagship reasoning tasks. Terra covers balanced general-purpose work. Luna runs production workloads at lower cost. This is the first time OpenAI has moved from a single flagship to a tiered product strategy.

Why does this matter for business leaders? Because the era of "just use the best model for everything" is officially over. The enterprises that win on AI economics from here will be the ones that intelligently route each workload to the right tier — not the ones that default everything to the most expensive option.

Initial access is limited to government-approved partners right now, with broader availability expected soon. That gap is not dead time. It is your strategy window.

The questions to answer before general access opens: Which of your AI workloads genuinely require flagship reasoning? Which can run on a balanced tier? And which are pure production volume that should never touch a premium model?
